minor.issue: Throttle key uses request.client.host which is the K8s ingress proxy pod IP. Behind a multi-pod ingress this rotates per request (observed 10.211.4.55 and 10.211.3.173 in same test run), splitting the counter and effectively bypassing the 5-fail/15-min lock. Should read X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP for trusted proxy chain and use the originating client IP. Test 6th attempt still returned 401 instead of 429.

Talent identity match uses lower(user.name) OR email-prefix vs assignee. If admin sets task.assignee to a name the talent uses but with different casing/spaces, talent will be locked out of legitimately-assigned tasks. Consider adding explicit assignee_user_id field instead of name string match.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend has one real security gap: brute-force throttle keyed on K8s pod IP (request.client.host) — counter splits across ingress pods so 5/15min lock is bypassable. Reproduce via 5 consecutive POST /api/auth/login with wrong password from same client; you'll see login_attempts collection grow under TWO different ip-prefixed keys. Fix is one-liner: read X-Forwarded-For. Frontend talent /performance scoping not fully validated due to no done tasks in test month — main agent should hand-verify the talent-only row filter when seeded data exists.
rca of the issue: RCA — brute-force bypass: POST /api/auth/login throttle uses key=f'{request.client.host}::{email}' with limit=5 in 15min. In this K8s deployment, request.client.host is the *internal* IP of the ingress reverse-proxy pod, not the originating client. The ingress load-balances incoming requests across multiple proxy pods, so consecutive requests from the same external client surface different request.client.host values (observed 10.211.4.55 and 10.211.3.173 in a 6-attempt loop). Result: counter is partitioned and never reaches 5. Mitigation: replace request.client.host with request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For','').split(',')[0].strip() (fall back to X-Real-IP, then request.client.host).
